comments.value:
While I agree Ranks are not the greatest idea, We forget we can hide our rank in the update and appear as normal User.

I personally, would rather have it setup like this, where your friends and favorites have a category in Safety settings rather than ranks.
Nuisance -> New user -> Verified User (Those that can upload) -> Friends -> Favorites. 
This is all you need to setup a proper safety system that is user controllable. Other Ranks are just excessive and like everyone says will start some sort of "higher Class" effect of social categorizing.

Just imagine the situation that only you are orange-colored and everybody else have purple-colored nametag. How weird it will be? It also be very weird if you are the only yellow(Veteran). 

There should have been better options like "hide everybody's rank(even for yourself)" or "troll or trustable". 

Additionally, most of the people who are using public avatar from avatar world(some of them contain fancy particles, though)don't need to be limited their avatar-features if mods do their work well.
Already had users block me and go away from or even friends unfriend me since I'm not high enough in the trust system also ppl tend to go away from me just BCS im a user

I agree with this post. It divides the userbase unecessarily which,in my opinion, would be the complete opposite on why people use it. VRChat is a social platform where people can freely communicate on an equal level. That, in my opinion, is the core of how people play VRChat. Doing this would make a divide, people who feel inferior and people who think they are more elite than everyone else due to just sinking a shit ton of hours. No offense to whoever thought of this ides probably felt like people needed a form of self validation. Let people feel like they dont have to prove themselves by crearing this social divide please. I already had someone join just to look at peoples colour and judge them.

I don't agree with what has been written, I find the system very useful. This is not about rewarding a person's ability or importance (except perhaps for the veteran), it's just about distinguishing new users from those who have been playing for a long time, which is a very different thing, this system tells you only people who have more experience and who are reliable from a new user and which, potentially, can turn out to be annoying or just a troll, but this doesn't mean that no one will talk more with users of lower rank, simply tells us to be more cautious. Not only that, but it pushes new users to improve and better behave with others to move up of rank instead of going around trolling people or annoying other users. Even for the veteran, I don't see anything bad, it's a way to reward users who have played a lot and contributed to the improvement of VRChat (or at least I think this is the criterion of judgment for veterans) and, as for other degrees, I see it more as an incentive for those who play to do better. Moreover if you don't like to show you higher rank than others you can also decide to "downgrade" to user, in case you worry about the fact that some may talk to you only for the color of the nametag. If then there are people who only look at the color of the nametag and don't want to talk to you maybe it's better that way, at least you avoid making friends who only look at "the importance" of a person more than the person himself :)

If people are being jerks over the trust system, just block, mute, or kick them out.

They will eventually drop down in rank accordingly.

The problem solves itself.

A trust system like this is so preferable to putting blanket restrictions on avatars and upload capabilities. I was afraid that they would start for example restricting custom shaders entirely or put very harsh limits on particles or physics because of the small minority of players that abuse the system.

Instead they have a system that as long as there are no exploits, it will moderate itself for a number of issues. This will free mods up to tackle problems manually, which is important due to it being such a small dev team that has no monetization available yet.

Veteran I think serves a purpose of pointing out players who are well-involved in the community. From what I saw in beta, vets were typically long-standing content creators or published tons of personal avatars combined with a massive amount of playtime and friends. I think it's helpful that newer players could know at a glance who to get direction from.
Personally I really like the colors. I feel like hanging out more to get higher ones. I wouldn’t like badges as much and it feels too much like a game.

@{5b1447490c6fe33c5d1370a2|full_name}: At the beginning of your post you say "This is not about rewarding a person's ability or performance" and then later in your post you go on to say "it's a way to reward users who have played a lot and contributed to the improvement of VRChat". Those statements completely contradict each other.

Why do we need 6 ranks to tell us who is new and who has been around longer? They exist, along with the colors, purely to boost people's egos.

@{5b6b4e8cb1b04a6db0be465d|full_name}: I think this is exactly the intent of VRChat devs, it's useless to hide it, people like to have a higher rank, but if this race to get the highest degree leads users to behave better to get it is really such a bad thing? And I must have expressed badly about the rankings, you have compared this system with CS:GO where the skill is rewarded, just do as many killings possible (or at least, I think so, I've never played it), and this can be achieved more or less quickly and doesn't require much effort and anyone can go to an higher rank, but here we talk about a system that not only based on the behavior you have with others, but also the time you spend in the game allows you to go up grade (or at least, I think I understand that it works like that), so you can spend like a year playing VRChat, but if you behave badly you're not going up with the rank and you get penalized because of the new safety system, as it should be, but who goes up of rank it's not a better or important person than the others, he simply behaved better and spent more time on VRChat. And yes, they have similar characteristics those 2 systems, in the end you just have to act in a certain way to get to a higher rank, with the only difference that on CS:GO anyone can get an higher rank, it doesn't matter if you are a troll or you just use some tricks to get higher and things like that, while for VRChat those who come to higher grades are only people who contribute positively to the game, and I don't speak of creating worlds or avatars, I also speak simply of behaving like a decent human, so like I said before, is it really so terrible to push users to behave well, even just changing the color of a nametag?

Then of course, this is my point of view, but I think it's wrong not to give at least a chance to this system, I think it has excellent potential

@{5b1447490c6fe33c5d1370a2|full_name}: But you don't know what the terms for ranking up is based on. This isn't going to encourage people to have good behavior, it's just going to encourage people to try and game the system. They'll randomly send out friend requests, upload absolute garbage maps, and leave the game on AFK. That's not an exaggeration either, I've already heard from people in-game that are doing this.

You say going up in rank is not a better or more important person, but that's exactly what it is. The ranks ascend in an upward, hierarchical fashion. Hell, even the description for veteran says it might be people who have created popular content. The fact that a rank is called "trusted" implies everything below it are users that are not to be trusted. A trusted person is better and more important than other users below it, they even get different privileges in the safety system.

I know people who have ban evaded in the past, or have multiple accounts that they ban evade and crash people on, and some of those people are trusted users, or veterans. The ranks quite frankly don't mean jack. They're completely arbitrary. At least with CS:GO the instructions to rank up are clear, but this game shouldn't even have any kind of ranking system in the first place. It's a social game, why on earth do we need special snowflake ranks and roles for people? They're not even ranks like "avatar creator" or "map creator", it's ranks that go in a direct, upward, hierarchical fashion. The rank on top is better, and is more important than every rank below it.

@{5b6b4e8cb1b04a6db0be465d|full_name}: Mh, I understand what you mean, but as I said before, I don't think it's a valid reason not to try this function. Remember that we are talking about a beta, it's clear that currently has flaws and (at least, hopefully) in the future will be improved to select users in a better way, and ignoring the fact that currently are selected people not very reliable the rest are all suppositions, maybe they are correct, but they are always suppositions. I mean, you talk about "wars between ranks" where those with the lowest rank will be completely ignored in the presence of a user with the highest level, garbage worlds, friendships sent to random people and AFK users, and honestly, it's so different from how is it now? lol

The users, even if now they don't have a visible rank, as soon as they recognize someone popular they run after them in every case, I have seen it a lot of times. Those who send random friend requests? This also happens to me often, and even if this happen, just refuse the request to those you don't know. The junk worlds, and I don't say this with the intent to offend anyone, but unfortunately there are already many, and for the AFK, as I said, I don't think the only factor to go up in rank is the time online, or at least, up to the User rank.

And then, honestly, even if it were that those of higher rank are important, who cares? Personally if I see that there are people doing drama on these things, I simply press the mute or block button. This system is designed so that players are moderating others and they decide who is a good user and who is not, so everything you're talking about can be easily solved by intervening, reporting and blocking these people, a system like this can be very useful to exclude these people, but as long as you add friends who have been banned and don't act when they do something wrong, it's clear that they rise in rank and the problem is not solved.
This is what you have wrought, devs. You've alienated more than half of your userbase. With every line of code you write, you destroy all hope of VR social experiences ever seeing the light of day.
Have any of you ever played an MMO? I have never seen anyone be elitist about levels that is worth talking to. You guys worry too much. If someone acts elitist, just immediately block them.

@{5b4eb6697a870c3a5c2b0ca5|full_name}: It is needed to display level on MMORPG. You have to find people who have similar level to co-operate. You don't need it from chatting. vrchat is not mmo rpg. it's social chat game. You will get rewarded from social interaction. 

there's 2 specific problem I certainly specify. 

(1) You can't prevent people from evading users who have low grades. 

You tell us to block them, but it's intended from system itself. 
"those people can be dangerous, so you can block theirs avatar-features and voice whatever you want, that is we recommend." You can't say someone who do this is elitist. The feature itself is elitist.

(2) It makes new-comer lose their interest.

Av new comer, who start vrchat right now, will be blocked his avatar-feature including voice, because he can be dangerous, even if he can't upload anything on vrchat server. 

By Avatar Safety setting Normal preset, his shaders will be blocked. 
By Maximum preset, his entire avatar will be blocked. still there's possibility left which somebody uses custom setting to block voices of him. 

If you want some reward system, you know, there's system called "Achievement". 

This system is currently mixed concept of rewarding and safety. Safety is not reward system. it's limit system we don't want to do but have to do it. The less we limit, the better we will get. Reward system is exactly opposite. it can't be mixed it up.
@{5b624a9c5667b3103cce300c|full_name}: I'm curious how you *know* that newcomers will lose interest? I'd like to know if people are new and can say hello/target them with positive social support :)

@{58c706f13b8e0378288be6e9|full_name}: About just displaying people who are new-comer, I didn't disagree with it. Trust system is not a just display or fancy badge. It limits availabilities of users and suggests that they can be dangerous.

I am curious if you will get motiavted when you are blocked by someone else.

I'd say keep nametag colors but repurpose them for marking friends and non-friends as well as hosts and moderators. Trust ranks could instead be indicated by a badge or title, something a little less conspicuous.

details:
Not only is it visually unappealing with all the cluster of different colored nametags now in a group of people, but it's almost like a caste system, where people are identified by their nametag color. I can only imagine this leading to drama and hurt feelings, and yes, drama will be caused even for something as small and stupid as giving people different colored names.

It's a social game and I don't really see the reason for people to be judged by their "rank" in a social game as if this was CS:GO or some similar game of a competitive nature. Keep the rank of the user under their nametag when you hover your cursor over them, but there's no reason to have them colored different names. If you're setting your trust and safety settings the way you want to anyway, you'd already know which users you do and don't want to see and the settings you have for them, so what's the point in even having the colors at that point? It's not really adding anything.
title: Nametag colors are a bad idea
